output.brief: The jump in DC-stage write-offs comes mainly from inside the DC, not from Haverlow. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four on 27 July, chilled pallets received at night wait a median of about 3 h 52 min before reaching the chambers, up from 44 min. The dock staging lanes are unrefrigerated and run 15–17°C overnight. Night write-off rate rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, Haverlow included, while the day shift stayed flat. Haverlow's trailer telematics show product at 2.4–3.5°C at door-open, and the chambers held temperature. The warm receiving probe readings are probably product that warmed on the dock. The probe values are keyed by hand, so I'd treat them with caution. Don't raise the chargeback or move volume. Restore the night team to six, cap dock-to-chamber time and monitor it weekly. Keep the receiving probe. Separately, Corriebank's credits rose after it moved to self-certified claims. That is a smaller part of the rise, and the evidence is only an association. Request their claim-level data and check a sample before changing their terms. I'm fairly confident in the main finding.
